span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repetition priming arises because processing an item changes the system, and the change facilitates later identification in proportion to how many of the same processes are re-invoked at test.

span.label: **A REVERSAL BETWEEN TWO TASKS ON THE SAME MATERIAL, WHICH IS WHY DIFFICULTY CANNOT EXPLAIN IT:** `Intramodal performance was superior in word identification, Quotation withheld.` Word-word beats picture-word when the task is identification; picture-word beats word-word when the task is recognition. **The sign flips, so no account in which one condition is simply weaker can survive** - the same structural move as Finkbeiner2011's colour-versus-identity and Schmidt2010's brightness-versus-contrast, and the strongest form of dissociation evidence in this corpus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND IT CONTRADICTS THE PROPOSITION IT SET OUT TO TEST.** Durso and Johnson (1979) held that although a printed word facilitates identification of a corresponding picture, a picture does NOT facilitate later word recognition. This paper finds that it does: `repetition priming of words by prior pictures IS FOUND with the PEST procedure, in which the dependent variable is accuracy of word identification.` **An asymmetry claimed in the literature turns out to be an artefact of the measure** - the authors say they used identification rather than naming latency `in order to avoid the range limitations in adult reading data`, and the effect appears
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE FIFTH EXPERIMENT EXISTS ONLY TO CROSS THE TWO TASKS, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN:** `Quotation withheld.` Four experiments establish the effect in one task; the fifth puts both tasks on the same footing so their ordering can be compared. **A crossover is only available to a design that runs both tasks** - and the earlier literature, which ran them separately, could not have found it however many subjects it used
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: word identification —contrasted-with→ episodic recognition
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE CONTRAST IS THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE SUBJECT.** These two tasks are crossed so that the ORDERING of intramodal against intermodal priming can be compared between them, and the reversal is what the fifth experiment was built to detect. Weight 0.95: the comparison is explicit and it is the paper's design. The reversal itself is quoted whole in the first sense, because it names `intramodal` and `intermodal` - which are not nodes here, since the staged text breaks `inter modal` in most of its occurrences.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: episodic recognition —operationalised-as→ memory trace
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — **`SUGGESTS` IS THE HEDGE AND IT IS IN THE SENTENCE THE QUOTE IS CUT FROM.** The distinct trace is an INFERENCE from the crossover, not a measurement - nothing in these experiments observes a trace. Weight 0.85 for that gap. What makes the inference strong rather than decorative is the shape of the evidence: a reversal cannot be produced by one trace read with more or less sensitivity, so a second representation is the cheapest account. The corpus should hold the inference and its distance from the data.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition priming —operationalised-as→ word identification
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THE MEASURE WAS CHOSEN TO AVOID A KNOWN CEILING AND THAT CHOICE PRODUCED THE RESULT.** The authors state they used word identification rather than naming latency `in order to avoid the range limitations in adult reading data` - and the effect Durso and Johnson could not find appears. Weight 0.9: the operationalisation is explicit, and the quote names both the procedure (PEST) and the two dependent variables (accuracy, threshold). **An operationalisation that changes the answer is worth an edge of its own**, because the disagreement in the literature is about the measure and not about the phenomenon.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
